title: Tokyo Cultural Guide: Emotion-Driven Exploration
description: A virtual cultural tour of LittlestTokyo guided by an animated face instructor. The user assigns emotional expressions to different district zones, links facial morph targets to environmental effects like lighting color and animation speed, and manages an undo/redo history of their teaching configurations. The goal is to create a coherent emotion-mapped tour that conserves a fixed 'energy budget' distributed across zones.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load LittlestTokyo.glb as the main environment scene and facecap.glb as a floating instructor head positioned in the upper-left of the viewport using a secondary orthographic overlay or fixed screen-space positioning. Setup: Use a PerspectiveCamera with OrbitControls targeting the Tokyo scene center. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights. Play the LittlestTokyo animation mixer at default speed. Display the facecap head with idle blinking. Core Mechanic: Divide the Tokyo scene into 5 named zones by bounding box regions (e.g., Station, Market, Temple, Park, Bridge). The user clicks a zone to select it, highlighted with a translucent colored box overlay. A UI panel shows 5 emotion sliders (happy, sad, angry, surprised, neutral) each 0-100. When the user adjusts sliders for a selected zone, the facecap model morphs to preview that expression in real-time. Confirming the assignment maps that emotion blend to the zone. Conservation Law: A total energy budget of 200 points is shared across all 5 zones. Each zone's slider sum counts toward this budget. The UI must show remaining budget and prevent exceeding it, redistributing excess proportionally if needed. Multi-Input Coupling: Each zone's dominant emotion affects its local directional light color (happy=warm yellow, sad=blue, angry=red, surprised=purple, neutral=white) and the Tokyo animation playback speed in that region (happy=1.5x, sad=0.5x, angry=2x, surprised=1.2x, neutral=1x). Undo/Redo: Maintain a stack of zone-emotion assignment states. Provide Undo and Redo buttons that restore previous configurations, updating all morph targets, lights, and speeds accordingly. Interaction Steps: select zone (1), adjust 5 sliders (2-6), confirm assignment (7), repeat for second zone (8-10), test undo (11), test redo (12). Show a top bar with zone name, budget remaining, and undo/redo buttons.
